Series API Reference¶

Back to PlussQit API Reference

This page documents pluss::Series — the numeric/boolean tensor object underneath numeric Timeline columns — one method page at a time, with real, compiled-and-run examples under every code block.

Using This Reference¶

  • Use the left sidebar to open one method page at a time. The method rail is intentionally alphabetized A-Z so it behaves like a fast lookup index rather than a tutorial sequence.

  • Each method page contains its signature(s), parameter details, a Gradient section for anything differentiable, verified output under every example, and working previous/next navigation.

  • This landing page stays intentionally short so the content panel is not one giant scroll of every method. Use the left sidebar as the primary lookup index, and see Series_Methods for the broader method naming-and-organization note.

Coverage¶

Series exposes a large public method surface, and this reference currently covers a working subset, prioritized by how load-bearing each family is (indexing/shape, factories, then the autodiff-sensitive family) rather than by code generation order. Every page here is real, hand-verified prose — nothing below is a mechanically generated stub.

The current handwritten shape and slice/indexing cluster now covers:

  • unary math core: abs, neg, sign, exp, log, sqrt, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, sinh, cosh, tanh, asinh, acosh, atanh

  • elementwise transforms and activations: expm1, log1p, reciprocal, sigmoid, relu

  • special functions: erf, erfc, lgamma

  • special functions II: digamma, polygamma, mvlgamma, erfinv, erfcinv, i0, sinc, igamma, igammac, zeta, beta (with betaln)

  • log-space & NaN-aware reductions: logsumexp, logcumsumexp, nansum, nanmean

  • running extrema: cummax, cummin

  • activations II: gelu, silu, softplus, leaky_relu, prelu, logit, hardshrink

  • probability normalization: softmax, log_softmax

  • broadcast & tiling: broadcast_to, expand, expand_as, repeat, tile, repeat_interleave

  • windowed / gather / difference: unfold, take_along_dim, narrow_copy, diff, ravel

  • pairwise (two-input) math: hypot, atan2, logaddexp, logaddexp2, xlogy, copysign, fmod, remainder, lerp, nextafter

  • elementwise II: fmax, fmin, heaviside, gcd, lcm, ldexp, frexp, float_power, floor_divide

  • distribution summaries: aminmax, count_nonzero, histogram

  • multivariate spread: cov, corrcoef

  • norm distance and constraint: dist, renorm

  • unary math II: rsqrt, square, abs2, cbrt, exp2, log2, log10, frac, deg2rad, rad2deg, signbit

  • number theory core: factor, is_prime, prime, factorial

  • grouped (segmented) reductions: grouped_sum, grouped_count, grouped_mean, grouped_min, grouped_max, grouped_var, grouped_std, grouped_median, grouped_mode

  • axis reordering: t, mT / adjoint, moveaxis / movedim, swapaxes / swapdims

  • complex numbers: real, imag, angle, conj, sgn

  • torch interop: tensor (the reverse of pluss::series::from_torch)

  • transport and materialization core: clone, contiguous, to

  • rounding and numeric-state helpers: ceil, floor, round, trunc, isnan, isinf, isfinite, invalid, invalid_index, nan_to_num

  • elementwise arithmetic core: add, sub, mul, div, pow

  • elementwise comparison core: eq, ne, lt, le, gt, ge

  • selection/counting core: select, count, nonzero, unique, isin, bincount, histc

  • ordering and rank selection: argsort, sort, topk, kthvalue

  • order statistics: median, nanmedian, mode, quantile, nanquantile

  • cyclic and planar rearrangement: flip, flipud, fliplr, roll, rot90

  • matrix diagonal and triangle core: trace, diag, diagonal, diag_embed, diagflat, diagonal_scatter, tril, tril_, triu, triu_

  • flat set logic core: union1d, unionize, intersect1d, intersection, setdiff1d, setxor1d, comp, cartprod

  • axis-wise set logic core: unionize_along, intersection_along, setdiff_along, setxor_along

  • shape, layout, dtype, and state introspection: size, sizes, dim, numel, stride, dtype, is_contiguous, platform predicates, dtype predicates, is_leaf, is_nonzero, is_same_size, and is_set_to

  • whole-Series and elementwise comparison: equal, allclose, and isclose, with exact shape-aware equality, broadcasted tolerance masks, and native C++ summary results

  • random sampling and stochastic fills: bernoulli, bernoulli_, multinomial, normal_, uniform_, random_, log_normal_, exponential_, geometric_, and cauchy_

  • view reshaping: view, reshape, transpose, permute, unsqueeze, squeeze, flatten

  • combine/build primitives: unite, pile

  • axis partitioning: chunk, split / split_with_sizes, tensor_split, unbind, hsplit / vsplit / dsplit

  • basic and dynamic selection: pos, slice, traverse_slice, block, extract, index

  • selector writes: traverse_put_, traverse_put, extract_put, extract_put_, index_put, index_put_

  • axis-slice indexed writes: index_add, index_add_, index_copy, index_copy_, index_fill, index_fill_, index_reduce, index_reduce_

  • flat gather/scatter primitives: take, put_

  • indexed write primitives: scatter, scatter_, scatter_add, scatter_add_, scatter_reduce, scatter_reduce_, scatter_reduce_sum, scatter_reduce_amax, scatter_reduce_amin, masked_fill, masked_fill_, masked_scatter, masked_scatter_, masked_select, where, where_

  • logical and bitwise masks: logical_and, logical_or, logical_xor, logical_not, logical_not_, bitwise_and, bitwise_or, bitwise_xor, bitwise_not

  • elementwise comparison/bounds helpers and a few load-bearing utility ops

  • reduction and scan core: sum, mean, prod, max, min, argmax, argmin, amax, amin, norm, cumsum, cumprod

  • autodiff and state controls: tracks_slope, tracks_slope_, reverse, detach, detach_, retain_grad, retains_grad, has_sensitivity, sensitivity, clear_sensitivity, storage_version

  • accessors: stat

  • linear-algebra accessor entrypoint: linearalg, with its complete product, determinant, transformation, factorization, norm, and solver surface documented in the dedicated accessor reference

  • antiderivative accessor entrypoint: antidiff, with its trapezoid and cumulative_trapezoid methods documented in the dedicated accessor reference

The complete handwritten SeriesStatAccessor reference covers:

  • descriptive reductions and higher moments

  • normal density and cumulative-distribution helpers

  • trailing-window summaries

  • centering, standardization, and row/column normalization

  • differentiable pairwise Euclidean distances

Accessors¶

Series has namespace-like accessors for related method families:

  • stat -> SeriesStatAccessor

  • linearalg -> SeriesLinearAlgAccessor

  • traverse -> SeriesTraverseAccessor

  • antidiff -> SeriesAntidiffAccessor

All four accessor references are complete across their public surfaces. Start with Series::stat, Series::linearalg, Series::traverse, or Series::antidiff for the entrypoint itself, or jump straight to a dedicated accessor reference from the sidebar. traverse is the value-driven search family — one call from a condition to the coordinates, matched values, and flat offsets of every position that satisfies it.
